question: Can even immense material wealth justify giving away this kaula teaching?
premises: One might possess wealth enough to fill the ocean with jewels
The verse sets up a comparison of worth
inference: Even wealth vast enough to fill the ocean with jewels is not a sufficient price for this teaching.
uncertainties: ratnasaṃpūrṇamakretuṃ is a fused and irregular form; exact verbal sense is unclear
plain_english: Even if one had an accumulation enough to fill the ocean with jewels...
